hero.intro_html: Everything that isn't the multi-year historical pilot deliverable lives here: the latest weekly conditions snapshot, a scrubbable month-by-month view of the last year, and structural-break detection over the raw (uncomposited) NDVI series. All three are data feeds, not finished alert products - the numbers below are published by hand whenever publish_site.py is re-run after a fresh local pass, not fetched live from the backend.

recent.title: Current conditions
recent.lede: Last ~2 months of Sentinel-2 data at weekly cadence, condensed into one composite: current NDVI/NDWI/NDMI plus a "% of the plot below the dry threshold" figure.
recent.quicklooks_lede: NDVI/NDWI/NDMI for the most recent usable weekly composite.

imagery.title: Monthly imagery, last year
imagery.lede: Whole-plot NDVI/NDWI/NDMI composites, scrub month by month - the same 12-month window as the Sector Explorer's "Last year" option, moved here since it's a single time series rather than a per-sector breakdown.

alerts.title: Vegetation break alerts
alerts.lede: A separate branch from the moisture monitoring above: every available raw Sentinel-2 scene over a chosen bounding box (no compositing), decomposed with STL (trend + season + remainder) and searched for changepoints with ruptures' PELT - the same conceptual approach BFAST (Verbesselt et al.) is built on, via GPU-free, pip-installable libraries. Treat detected breaks as candidates to investigate, not calibrated alerts.
alerts.table_lede: Each row is one detected changepoint in the trend component: the fitted trend level in the ~3 months before vs. after, and the resulting delta.
alerts.note_html: Pilot/precursor output across this whole page - none of these thresholds are calibrated against field data yet. BFAST-style, not the literal BFAST/R package. Bounding box, lookback window, and penalty scale are all set in config.py (ALERT_BBOX, ALERT_YEARS, BFAST_PENALTY_SCALE). Natural next step (see README): turn the recent-conditions feed into a scheduled job that persists each run and diffs against the previous one to generate real alerts.
